notes: Fiscal year ended December 28, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Filings: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0000050863-25-000009) and 2025 proxy statement (accession 0000050863-25-000054), both read on www.sec.gov. GORDON MOORE is deceased. The 2025 proxy's ownership table lists only directors, NEOs, Vanguard and BlackRock; it shows no Moore estate, trust or Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation holding, and 'Moore' appears in the 10-K only as Moore's Law. Family is therefore null. BUYBACKS: zero. The cash-flow statement has no repurchase line for 2024, and the 10-K says the last repurchase was in Q1 2021. The only share-related outflow, $631 million of restricted stock unit withholdings, is not a buyback. DIVIDENDS: Intel suspended its dividend from Q4 2024. STOCK COMP: Intel tags no separate note total; the $3,410 million is the cash-flow add-back, matching the total of the share-based compensation line in the segment note. HOLDERS: the proxy says the 5% holdings are 'as of December 31, 2024', but it cites 13G/A filings dated January and February 2024, which normally report end-of-2023 holdings. Because of this conflict, asOf is null.

footprint.notes: Intel publishes no 50-state breakdown; its April 2025 U.S. fact sheet (company-hosted PDF) gives investment figures for its four manufacturing states only (Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio), and the newer live usachipmaking page has slightly updated numbers ($65B Oregon, $34.5B Arizona, $17.68B New Mexico) plus state GDP contributions; the fact sheet is used because it is closest to the Dec 2024 snapshot. Cumulative investment and new-project figures are different measures and must not be added. The fact sheet also lists CHIPS Act awards per state (AZ $3.94B, NM $500M, OR $1.86B, OH $1.5B); these are government funding to Intel, not Intel's footprint, and are not recorded. Nationally, the fact sheet says Intel has 45,000 U.S.-based employees (company-published; 10-K total workforce 108,900); not recorded as a row because the U.S. row's source is the 10-K PP&E table. A 2021 third-party study ("Intel's Impacts on the US Economy", FY2019 data) covering AZ, CA, NM and OR exists but is far older than the snapshot and was not used. 10-K Properties gives only square feet: U.S. 38 million (35 owned, 3 leased) vs other countries 32 million; there are no per-state or per-country site counts, and the manufacturing countries are listed without figures, so they appear as sites. Ohio fab completion has been slowed and Germany/Poland projects put on hold (10-K).
